To deploy a WordPress application on Kubernetes, you will need to create a Kubernetes manifest file, which describes the desired state of the deployment. Here is an example of a Kubernetes YAML manifest file for deploying a WordPress application:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
name: wordpress
labels:
app: wordpress
spec:
replicas: 1
selector:
matchLabels:
app: wordpress
template:
metadata:
labels:
app: wordpress
spec:
containers:
- name: wordpress
image: wordpress
ports:
- containerPort: 80
env:
WORDPRESS\_DB\_HOST: mysql
WORDPRESS\_DB\_USER: wordpress
WORDPRESS\_DB\_PASSWORD: wordpress
WORDPRESS\_DB\_NAME: wordpress
volumes:
- name: wordpress-data
persistentVolumeClaim:
claimName: wordpress-pvc
This manifest creates a deployment called "wordpress" with a single replica. It uses a container image for WordPress, sets the container ports for HTTP and MySQL, and sets environment variables for the WordPress database. It also creates a persistent volume claim for storing data from the WordPress application.
Please note that this is a basic example, you may need to adjust it based on your specific requirements.
